title: Speak JSON
brief: Your CRM integration parses Granite's response with json.loads(). Extract the sender's name, company, requested meeting date (YYYY-MM-DD), and topic. The output must be valid JSON and nothing else.

lesson.summary: When code consumes the output, the prompt is an API contract. Specify the exact schema and value formats, and forbid any extra text. One example object is worth a paragraph of description.
lesson.why_it_matters: Most enterprise LLM integrations (CRM enrichment, ticket routing, document extraction) fail not because the model is wrong, but because the output can't be parsed.
lesson.weak_example: Get the important info from this email: {{email}}
lesson.strong_example:
Return ONLY a JSON object with keys name, company, meeting_date (YYYY-MM-DD), topic. No other text.

<email>{{email}}</email>

rubric: The topic field captures the purpose of the email in a short, accurate phrase
hints: Imagine a program, not a person, reading the output. What would make json.loads() fail?
This is about structured output. Name the exact keys and the format of each value (dates especially), and forbid anything outside the JSON: no greetings, no explanations, no markdown.
Try: 'Return ONLY a JSON object with keys "name", "company", "meeting_date" (YYYY-MM-DD), "topic". No markdown, no extra text.' Including one example JSON object helps even more.
reference_prompt:
Extract meeting request details from the email between the <email> tags.

Return ONLY a valid JSON object with exactly these keys:
- "name": the sender's full name
- "company": the sender's company
- "meeting_date": the requested date in YYYY-MM-DD format
- "topic": the purpose of the meeting in under 10 words

Example output:
{"name": "Ana Silva", "company": "Acme Corp", "meeting_date": "2026-01-15", "topic": "Pricing review for enterprise plan"}

Do not include any text, markdown, or explanation outside the JSON.

<email>
{{email}}
</email>
